renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: Love, thought, and joy for him swell like a thousand streams. We bow to the Lord who wears wise minds like a garland. Remembering him is the one cure for not-knowing, so we beg him to grant its gift. He fulfills every aim men have, so even our bow belongs to him.

We fished loves jewel-stone from the dread sea, so nothing is unwon. Few truly know him, veiled and unveiled. With no needs and no traits he still wins, unborn, the top fruit of all wants. His is the milk-sea fortune, his alone by birthright. He blooms for our release and guards in life and beyond it. He knows all, makes all, is all -- so all we have goes to the endless.

renders.prompt: Render the argument of this song in a Gen-Z voice: direct, a little feral, zero cringe, no slang overload. Keep every doctrinal claim intact — voice changes, content does not. No new doctrines, no comparisons, no meta-commentary, no quoted terms.

paragraphs.text: Worshipped, pondered, pleased -- that vibe swells thousandfold toward him. Bow to the chief wreathed in bright minds. Recall of him is the sole cure for the dumb dark, so we ask the dose. He cashes out every human aim, so even the bow is his already.

Hooked loves gem from the horror ocean -- all won. Barely anyone sees him, hid and shown. Want-free, trait-free, still taking it all, unborn top prize of every craving. Milk-ocean estate, his by blood alone. He blooms us loose and covers us breathing or not. All-knowing, all-making, all -- everything filed under endless.
